output.explanation: paypal.js fell back to a hardcoded client id and client secret whenever PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID or PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET was unset. That put the secret in git history and let a misconfigured deploy run quietly on the baked-in account. Both values now come only from the environment, and the module throws a clear error at startup if either is missing.

edits.find:
const PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID = process.env.PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID || "kiln-sandbox-client";
const PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET = process.env.PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET || "kiln-sandbox-secret-2024";

output.notes: Rotate the PayPal client secret that was committed ("kiln-sandbox-secret-2024") in the PayPal developer dashboard, because it stays in git history. Make sure PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID and PAYPAL_CLIENT_SECRET are set in every environment, including local dev and CI. paypal.js throws when server.js imports it, so the server will now refuse to start if either one is missing.
